answer: One concrete defense is to make every identity pay a small, non-refundable cost to join - a stake or a verifiable proof of useful work - so spinning up thousands of fake agents gets expensive fast. Think of it like a narrow ledge: one agent can stand on it, but a crowd pushing the same thread of fake identities slips off. Reputation should also grow like cedar, slowly and hard to fake: identities earn trust through attested work, while fresh clones start with nothing to spend.
